description:
Filed by s527c (2026-10-31), found by t/op/for.t's first companion run (the file had been a whole-file PPI failure until s527c, #1580).  SILENT WRONG, pre-existing (main ff5f72b5 + vendor dc242138 = the s527c tree): `local *NAME` does NOT hide a scalar that an enclosing `local $NAME = ...` gave a value -- inside the glob-local scope $NAME still reads the outer local's value; perl reads a fresh (undef) scalar.

perl 5.40.3 vs PCL:
  our $foo = "boo"; { local *foo; print defined $foo ? "def [$foo]\n" : "undef\n"; }    perl: undef   PCL: undef   (control: a plain package value IS hidden)
  local $bar = "b"; { local *bar; print defined $bar ? "def [$bar]\n" : "undef\n"; }    perl: undef   PCL: def [b]
  { local $foo = "boo"; { local *foo; for $foo (1,2) {} print defined $foo ? "def\n" : "undef\n"; } }   perl: undef   PCL: def  (t/op/for.t 111 "NULL GvSV", 112 "NULL GvSV int iterator")

Suspect: `local $NAME` dynamically binds the scalar CELL (a let of the special variable), and `local *NAME` swaps the glob's scalar SLOT -- a read of $NAME inside reaches the let-bound value, not the glob's new empty slot.  Cheap discriminating measurement: pl2cl the second line and read whether `local $bar` lowers to a dynamic binding of the cell symbol and `local *bar` to p-local-glob on the glob -- two different places.  ir-spec §7.2 (globs) is the normative text to check.
subject: local *NAME does not hide a scalar an enclosing local $NAME = ... set: $NAME keeps the outer local's value inside the glob-local scope (op/for.t NULL GvSV rows) -- silent wrong
